Best Wineries to Visit in Sedona & Verde Valley: A Local Guide

Just two hours north of Phoenix, Arizona's Verde Valley wine region has emerged as a world-class destination. With over 30 wineries and tasting rooms, here's your guide to the best experiences.

Best Wineries to Visit in Sedona & Verde Valley

Just two hours north of Phoenix, Arizona's Verde Valley wine region has emerged as a world-class destination. With over 30 wineries and tasting rooms, here's your guide to the best experiences.

Top Wineries by Experience

Page Springs Cellars

The pioneer of Arizona wine

Founded in 2004, this winery set the standard for the region. The tasting room overlooks Oak Creek, and the wines consistently earn national recognition.

Must try: Petite Sirah, Rhône blends
Atmosphere: Rustic, knowledgeable staff
Food: Cheese boards, charcuterie

Javelina Leap Vineyard & Winery

Family-friendly with stunning views

Located on a hilltop with panoramic views of the valley, Javelina Leap offers a relaxed atmosphere perfect for groups.

Must try: Zinfandel, Syrah
Atmosphere: Casual, picnic-friendly
Food: Food trucks on weekends

Alcantara Vineyards

Tuscan vibes in Arizona

Beautiful Italian-inspired architecture with expansive grounds for private events. Popular for weddings and corporate gatherings.

Must try: Super Tuscan blends
Atmosphere: Upscale, romantic
Food: Full restaurant on-site

Burning Tree Cellars

Artisan winemaking

Small-batch production focused on quality over quantity. Intimate tasting experiences with the winemaker often available.

Must try: Viognier, Grenache
Atmosphere: Boutique, educational

Pillsbury Wine Company

Urban tasting room in Cottonwood

Sam Pillsbury, a filmmaker-turned-winemaker, creates bold wines with story and personality.

Must try: Roan Red, Picpoul Blanc
Atmosphere: Artistic, quirky

Suggested Itinerary

Half-day (4 hours)

  • 2-3 wineries
  • Light lunch at one venue
  • Perfect for first-timers

Full-day (7-8 hours)

  • 4-5 wineries
  • Leisurely pace with lunch
  • Comprehensive experience

Best Times to Visit

  • Spring (March-May): Wildflowers, comfortable temperatures
  • Fall (September-November): Harvest season, grape crushing
  • Winter: Fewer crowds, cozy tastings
